summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop: autoscaler misclassification of ephemeral fanout leads to NVLink saturation and elevated p99
description:
Issue summary:
BrightWrite reported sudden p50/p99 throughput drop and elevated tail latency on their dedicated fleet during a 25-minute window. Traffic profile showed a sharp rise in many short-lived connections (ephemeral fanout) from a new internal worker pool. The autoscaler classified the ephemeral fanout as sustained coldstart activity, delayed scale-up decisions, and the scheduler routed more short streams to a subset of GPUs which saturated NVLink and increased kernel queuing.

Impact:
- Customer observed 4x p99 generation latency and 60% drop in sustained throughput for reserved pool routes.
- Affected customers had degraded UX for chat sessions and some 5xx retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: BrightWrite-reserved-01
- Region: us-west-2 primary (failover to us-east-1 unaffected)
- Runtime: redwood-serving v2.14.1
- Autoscaler: predictive policy v1.3.4

Observed metrics and timeline:
- 2026-03-10T13:02 UTC: fanout spike begins (many short connections, median duration 2.3s)
- 13:05–13:25: NVLink utilization on GPU set A rose from 18% to 92%
- 13:06: scheduler attach latency increased; kernel queue length grew, kernel-queue-wait p95 spiked
- 13:10: autoscaler misclassified load pattern and did not provision extra GPUs until 13:20
- 13:27: throughput recovered after manual intervention and temporary routing change
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Recreate many short-lived parallel streams targetting the dedicated route (e.g., 3000 connections/min with median request length 200 tokens and keepalive 2-5s).
2. Ensure traffic targets the same small set of model variants and the same GPU stripe to mimic affinity.
3. Observe NVLink utilization, kernel queue length, and autoscaler decisions for 15–30 minutes.
4. Verify autoscaler classification metric (pod_attach_duration, connection_duration_histogram) and predictive window outputs.
comments: Support (Aisha): Logged by BrightWrite CS at 2026-03-10 13:30 UTC — reported sharp latency increase on dedicated route BrightWrite-reserved-01.
SRE (Luca): Triage started. Captured GPU telemetry and traced NVLink saturation pattern. Suspect short-lived fanout causing affinity concentration.
Eng (Marina): Noticed autoscaler predictive model treats many short-lived connections as noise; thresholding logic kept it from reacting.
Support (Aisha): Customer confirms they deployed a new worker pool around 12:58 UTC sending rapid short streams.
SRE (Luca): Temporarily rerouted a percentage of traffic to neighbor pool and manually increased GPU allocation at 13:20; throughput normalized by 13:27.
investigation_notes: Telemetry shows disproportionate attach events concentrated on 4 GPUs within the reserved stripe leading to NVLink hot spots.
Autoscaler decision logs show sliding-window score remained below reactive threshold due to median connection duration below configured min_duration parameter (default 5s).
Kernel queue metrics align with sustained NVLink saturation — the runtime serializes certain collective ops when NVLink is congested, exacerbating p99 latency.
We observed affinity decay: many short-lived streams reuse same socket pins causing scheduler to prefer GPUs with existing cached KV entries, worsening imbalance.
Cross-check with observability: no driver crashes or OOMs; errors were timeouts and increased 5xx retries from client library.
resolution: Immediate workaround: manually increased reserved GPU count for BrightWrite-reserved-01 and applied traffic-split rule to spread new connections across 3 additional stripes at 13:18 UTC.
Customer workaround recommended: throttle aggregator so new worker pool staggers connection bursts or increase keepalive to exceed autoscaler min_duration.

Root cause: autoscaler classification threshold too conservative for workloads with many short sessions; combined with scheduler affinity heuristics this produced NVLink hot spots and kernel queueing.

Long-term fixes: (1) adjust autoscaler to include high-connection-rate signals (attach_rate) in predictive model; (2) scheduler to consider NVLink usage when assigning new short-lived streams; (3) introduce short-session mitigation route that uses round-robin GPU selection; (4) add automated mitigation playbook in runbook.

Follow-ups: related GH PR to change autoscaler scoring (github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4821), scheduler NVLink-aware allocator spike (github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1289), and a Confluence postmortem link added.
resolution_status: Workaround applied; pending code changes and follow-up verification
notes: Playbook updated to include attach_rate check for predictive autoscaler.
Customer requested weekly updates until fixes land; assigned to Solutions Eng for customer communication.
